issues.title: [BUG] AI SDK v5 Memory Type Compatibility (example error)
issues.body:
## Describe the Bug

There is a type incompatibility between Mastra's `UIMessageWithMetadata` type and AI SDK v5's `UIMessage` type when used as a return type in API routes. The root cause is that `UIMessageWithMetadata` is explicitly defined as an AI SDK v4 type, not v5.

The type is defined here: https://github.com/mastra-ai/mastra/blob/dc099b40fb31147ba3f362f98d991892033c4c67/packages/core/src/agent/message-list/index.ts#L78

## Steps To Reproduce

1. cd `examples/ai-sdk-v5`
2. Install AI SDK v5 (`ai@^5.0.52`)
3. Import `UIMessage` from `ai` in the API route `examples/ai-sdk-v5/app/api/initial-chat/route.ts`
4. Try to return `result?.uiMessages` from `memory.query()` as a `UIMessage[]` type
5. TypeScript will throw the compatibility error
Example code:
```typescript
import { mastra } from "@/src/mastra";
import { NextResponse } from "next/server";
import { UIMessage } from "ai";

const myAgent = mastra.getAgent("weatherAgent");
export async function GET(): Promise<NextResponse<UIMessage[]>> {
  const memory = await myAgent.getMemory();
  const result = await memory?.query({
    threadId: "2",
  });

  return NextResponse.json(result?.uiMessages || []); // ts-error here
}
```

```
./app/api/initial-chat/route.ts:12:3
Type error: Type 'NextResponse<UIMessageWithMetadata[]>' is not assignable to type 'NextResponse<UIMessage<unknown, UIDataTypes, UITools>[]>'.
  Type 'UIMessageWithMetadata[]' is not assignable to type 'UIMessage<unknown, UIDataTypes, UITools>[]'.
    Type 'UIMessageWithMetadata' is not assignable to type 'UIMessage<unknown, UIDataTypes, UITools>'.
      Types of property 'role' are incompatible.
        Type '"data" | "user" | "assistant" | "system"' is not assignable to type '"user" | "assistant" | "system"'.
          Type '"data"' is not assignable to type '"user" | "assistant" | "system"'.

  10 |   });
  11 |
> 12 |   return NextResponse.json(result?.uiMessages || []);
     |   ^
  13 | }
  14 |
```

Reproduction commit available at: https://github.com/mastra-ai/mastra/commit/6ec5a6b5f2b01735fe59cbed724f61fce993802b

## Expected Behavior

`UIMessageWithMetadata` should be compatible with AI SDK v5's `UIMessage` type, or there should be a clear migration path/adapter. The type definition should be updated to support AI SDK v5.

## Environment Information

- Mastra Version: latest
- Node.js Version: v22.16.0
- AI SDK Version: v5.0.52
- TypeScript: latest
- OS: macOS/Linux/Windows

## Verification

- [x] I have searched the existing issues to make sure this is not a duplicate (similar to #7686 but specific to memory)
- [x] I have included sufficient information for the team to reproduce and understand the issue

issues.title: [BUG]  Agent.streamVNext throws 'Unknown error' instead of real error details when execution fails
issues.body:
### Describe the Bug



**Agent.streamVNext and resumeStreamVNext throw generic "Unknown error" messages instead of providing real error details when execution fails, making debugging extremely difficult for users.**

### Current Behavior
When `Agent.streamVNext` or `resumeStreamVNext` fails internally, users receive a generic error:

```javascript
FAILED: MastraError: Unknown error
    at Agent.streamVNext (file:///path/to/agent.ts:3419:15)
    ...
  id: 'AGENT_STREAM_VNEXT_FAILED',
  domain: 'AGENT',
  category: 'USER',
  details: { error: undefined },
  [cause]: undefined
}
```

### Expected Behavior
Users should see the actual underlying error details, such as:

```javascript
FAILED: MastraError: Error: password authentication failed for user "postgres"
    at PostgresStore.init (file:///path/to/storage.ts:202:13)
    ...
  id: 'AGENT_STREAM_VNEXT_FAILED',
  domain: 'AGENT',
  category: 'USER',
  details: {
    error: 'Error: password authentication failed for user "postgres"\n' +
      '    at PostgresStore.init (file:///path/to/storage.ts:202:13)\n' +
      '    ...',
    stack: 'Error: password authentication failed...',
    code: 'ECONNREFUSED'
  },
  [cause]: Error: password authentication failed for user "postgres"
      at PostgresStore.init (file:///path/to/storage.ts:202:13)
      ...
}
```

### Impact
- **Debugging**: Users cannot identify the root cause of failures
- **Database Issues**: PostgresStore connection errors are masked
- **Edge Cases**: Supabase Edge + PostgresStore compatibility issues are hidden
- **Developer Experience**: Significantly reduced debugging capabilities

### Root Cause
The error handling code uses `result.error.message` directly, which can be undefined:

```typescript
// Current problematic code
throw new MastraError({
  id: 'AGENT_STREAM_VNEXT_FAILED',
  domain: ErrorDomain.AGENT,
  category: ErrorCategory.USER,
  text: result.error.message,  // Could be undefined!
  details: {
    error: result.error.message,  // Could be undefined!
  },
});
```

### Steps to Reproduce
1. Create an Agent with Memory + PostgresStore
2. Use an invalid database connection string
3. Call `agent.generateVNext()` with memory options
4. Observe generic "Unknown error" instead of real error details

### Environment
- **Package**: `@mastra/core`
- **Methods**: `Agent.streamVNext`, `Agent.resumeStreamVNext`
- **Storage**: `PostgresStore` (any storage that can fail)
- **Runtime**: Node.js, Deno Edge (Supabase Functions)

This bug affects all users trying to debug Agent execution failures, particularly those using PostgresStore in edge environments.

### Steps To Reproduce


### 1. Setup Environment
```bash
# Install required packages
npm i @mastra/core @mastra/memory @mastra/pg @ai-sdk/google ai
```

### 2. Create Test File
Create `repro-bug.mjs`:
```javascript
import { Agent } from '@mastra/core/agent';
import { Memory } from '@mastra/memory';
import { PostgresStore } from '@mastra/pg';
import { createGoogleGenerativeAI } from '@ai-sdk/google';

// Intentionally invalid database URL to trigger connection failure
const DATABASE_URL = 'postgresql://invalid:invalid@invalid-host:5432/invalid-db?sslmode=require';
const GOOGLE_GENERATIVE_AI_API_KEY = 'YOUR_GOOGLE_API_KEY';

const google = createGoogleGenerativeAI({ apiKey: GOOGLE_GENERATIVE_AI_API_KEY });

const memory = new Memory({
  storage: new PostgresStore({ connectionString: DATABASE_URL }),
});

const agent = new Agent({
  name: 'test-agent',
  description: 'Test agent for bug reproduction',
  instructions: 'Always be helpful.',
  model: google('gemini-1.5-flash'),
  memory,
});
```

### 3. Trigger the Bug
```javascript
async function reproduceBug() {
  console.log('--- Reproducing Agent.streamVNext bug ---');
  try {
    const res = await agent.generateVNext("Hello, test message", {
      format: 'aisdk',
      memory: { resource: 'test', thread: 'test' },
      onError: e => console.error('onError:', e?.message || e),
    });
    console.log('Result text:', res.text);
  } catch (e) {
    console.error('FAILED:', e);
  }
}

reproduceBug().catch(err => console.error('Fatal error:', err));
```

### 4. Run the Test
```bash
node repro-bug.mjs
```

### 5. Observe the Bug
**Expected Output (showing the bug):**
```
--- Reproducing Agent.streamVNext bug ---
Error executing step prepare-memory-step: Error: getaddrinfo ENOTFOUND invalid-host
    at PostgresStore.init (file:///path/to/storage.ts:202:13)
    ...
FAILED: MastraError: Unknown error
    at Agent.streamVNext (file:///path/to/agent.ts:3419:15)
    ...
  id: 'AGENT_STREAM_VNEXT_FAILED',
  domain: 'AGENT',
  category: 'USER',
  details: { error: undefined },
  [cause]: undefined
}
```

### 6. Alternative Reproduction (Database Auth Error)
Use a valid hostname but invalid credentials:
```javascript
const DATABASE_URL = 'postgresql://wronguser:wrongpass@localhost:5432/wrongdb?sslmode=require';
```

**Expected Output:**
```
Error executing step prepare-memory-step: Error: password authentication failed for user "wronguser"
    at PostgresStore.init (file:///path/to/storage.ts:202:13)
    ...
FAILED: MastraError: Unknown error
    at Agent.streamVNext (file:///path/to/agent.ts:3419:15)
    ...
  details: { error: undefined },
  [cause]: undefined
}
```

### 7. Verify the Bug
- ✅ **Bug Confirmed**: If you see "Unknown error" with `details: { error: undefined }`
- ❌ **Bug Fixed**: If you see the real error message like "getaddrinfo ENOTFOUND invalid-host"

### 8. Additional Test Cases
Test with different failure scenarios:
- **Invalid hostname**: `postgresql://user:pass@nonexistent-host:5432/db`
- **Wrong credentials**: `postgresql://wronguser:wrongpass@localhost:5432/db`
- **Wrong port**: `postgresql://user:pass@localhost:9999/db`
- **Invalid SSL**: `postgresql://user:pass@localhost:5432/db?sslmode=require` (when server doesn't support SSL)

All these scenarios should show the **real error details** instead of generic "Unknown error" messages.

### Expected Behavior

**Users should see the real error details instead of "Unknown error":**

```javascript
// Instead of this:
FAILED: MastraError: Unknown error
  details: { error: undefined }

// Users should see this:
FAILED: MastraError: Error: getaddrinfo ENOTFOUND invalid-host
  details: {
    error: 'Error: getaddrinfo ENOTFOUND invalid-host\n    at PostgresStore.init...',
    stack: 'Error: getaddrinfo ENOTFOUND invalid-host\n    at PostgresStore.init...',
    code: 'ENOTFOUND'
  },
  [cause]: Error: getaddrinfo ENOTFOUND invalid-host
}
```

issues.body: Description Despite the memory/config explicitly disabling title generation, titles continue to be auto-created and the memory/inspector view reflects generateTitle as enabled. Impact • Confusing/incorrect conversation metadata. • Breaks consumers relying on generateTitle: false to suppress auto-titling for compliance or UX reasons. Steps to Reproduce 1. Configure an agent with generateTitle: false at the agent level (and/or within its memory config). const agent = createAgent({ // ... memory: { generateTitle: false, // other memory settings }, }); 2. Build and run locally in dev/prod mode. 3. Start any conversation and end a turn. 4. Inspect the conversation metadata/memory (via logs or inspector). Expected Behavior • No title is generated for the conversation. • Memory/inspector shows generateTitle: false. Actual Behavior • A title is still generated. • Memory/inspector (or runtime dump) shows generateTitle: true or otherwise indicates it is enabled. Additional Notes / Observations • Reproducible “heavily” on local with production/development build. • Appears related to memory/config merging or defaults overriding explicit agent-level value. Workarounds Tried • Forcing generateTitle: false at multiple levels (agent + memory) — still generates titles. • Sisabled memory all togather. Environment • mastra.ai version: lates Acceptance Criteria • When generateTitle: false is set at the agent (or memory) level: • No conversation titles are auto-generated. • Inspector/logs accurately reflect generateTitle: false. • Config precedence documented: agent-level explicitly overrides defaults/globals. • Regression test added to prevent future overrides during config merge/hydration. ## Description

Refactors structured output validation to fix issues with Bedrock and LMStudio models.

1. **Moved validation from `flush()` to `text-end` chunk** - Validate at the correct point in stream
lifecycle

linked_prs.body: Fixes a validation bug where tools would reject valid LLM responses because validation used the original Zod schema while the LLM received a schema-compat transformed version. This caused issues with OpenAI o3 reasoning models (which convert `.optional()` to `.nullable()` and send `null` values) and Claude 3.5 Haiku (which strips `min`/`max` string constraints). Validation would reject these responses even though they matched what the LLM was told was valid. The fix restructures `CoreToolBuilder.build()` to apply schema compatibility before creating the execute function, then passes the processed Zod schema to `createExecute()` for validation. Now validation uses the same schema that was sent to the LLM. Added comprehensive tests covering Anthropic string constraints, OpenAI o3 nullable conversion, and the specific `updateWorkingMemory` bug that triggered this investigation. Before: After: Fixes https://github.com/mastra-ai/mastra/issues/8805

issues.title: [BUG] Repeated assistant messages when integrating with AI SDKs useChat
issues.body:
### Describe the Bug

This is a well known issue in AI SDK UI that has a solution suggested here:

https://ai-sdk.dev/docs/troubleshooting/repeated-assistant-messages#repeated-assistant-messages-in-usechat

The issue arises when using client-side tool calls with `addToolResult` where after each such tool call a new message is created and it contains everything already present in the previous message. In AI SDK that's resolved by passing in `originalMessages`.

I'm using `@mastra/ai-sdk` and I can't find an option to do such a thing there:
```
server: {
    apiRoutes: [
      chatRoute({
        path: '/chat',
        agent: 'uiAgent',
      }),
    ],
  },
```

### Steps To Reproduce

- Create a Mastra agent and expose it so it's AI SDK compatible via `@mastra/ai-sdk`
- Add a client-side tool to the agent
- Create a React app and add the AI SDK UI to it
- `useChat` hook needs to be configured with `sendAutomaticallyWhen: lastAssistantMessageIsCompleteWithToolCalls`
- On `onToolCall` run `addToolResult()` to add a result to your tool call

Observe the rendered messages, everything before and including the client side tool call will end up in a new message as well so that the content is duplicated.

**Client side tool calls that don't provide outputs by calling `addToolResult()` are not affected.**

Open AI is the provider and the same thing happens regardless of the model used but I have tested with 4o extensively, and with GPT-5 it's difficult to test because of  https://github.com/mastra-ai/mastra/issues/8665

### Expected Behavior

No messages with duplicated content.

### Environment Information

Deps:
```
    "@ai-sdk/openai": "2.0.52",
    "@mastra/ai-sdk": "0.1.1",
    "@mastra/core": "0.20.2",
    "@mastra/libsql": "0.15.1",
    "@mastra/loggers": "0.10.15",
    "@mastra/memory": "0.15.6",
```
UI:
```
    "@ai-sdk/react": "2.0.71",
    "ai": "5.0.71",
```

Mac OS 15.7.1/MBP 16" M1 Pro

- [x] I have included sufficient information for the team to reproduce and understand the issue

## @mastra/core@0.21.2-alpha.0

### Patch Changes

-   Update provider registry and model documentation with latest models and providers ([`c67ca32`](https://github.com/mastra-ai/mastra/commit/c67ca32e3c2cf69bfc146580770c720220ca44ac))

-   Add deprecation warnings for format:ai-sdk ([#9018](https://github.com/mastra-ai/mastra/pull/9018))

-   network routing agent text delta ai-sdk streaming ([#8979](https://github.com/mastra-ai/mastra/pull/8979))

-   Support writing custom top level stream chunks ([#8922](https://github.com/mastra-ai/mastra/pull/8922))

-   fix(core): Fix Gemini message ordering validation errors (#7287, #8053) ([#8069](https://github.com/mastra-ai/mastra/pull/8069))

    Fixes Gemini API "single turn requests" validation error by ensuring the first non-system message is from the user role. This resolves errors when:

    -   Messages start with assistant role (e.g., from memory truncation)
    -   Tool-call sequences begin with assistant messages

    **Breaking Change**: Empty or system-only message lists now throw an error instead of adding a placeholder user message, preventing confusing LLM responses.

    This fix handles both issue #7287 (tool-call ordering) and #8053 (single-turn validation) by inserting a placeholder user message when needed.

-   fix(core): Validate structured output at text-end instead of flush ([#8934](https://github.com/mastra-ai/mastra/pull/8934))

    Fixes structured output validation for Bedrock and LMStudio by moving validation from `flush()` to `text-end` chunk. Eliminates `finishReason` heuristics, adds special token extraction for LMStudio, and validates at the correct point in stream lifecycle.

-   fix model.loop.test.ts tests to use structuredOutput.schema and add assertions ([#8926](https://github.com/mastra-ai/mastra/pull/8926))

-   When using OpenAI models with JSON response format, automatically enable strict schema validation. ([#8924](https://github.com/mastra-ai/mastra/pull/8924))

-   Added the ability to use model router configs for embedders (eg "openai/text-embedding-ada-002") ([#8992](https://github.com/mastra-ai/mastra/pull/8992))

-   Always set supportsStructuredOutputs true for openai compatible provider. ([#8933](https://github.com/mastra-ai/mastra/pull/8933))

-   Support for custom resume labels mapping to step to be resumed ([#8941](https://github.com/mastra-ai/mastra/pull/8941))

-   Fixed an issue where a custom URL in model router still validated unknown providers against the known providers list. Custom URL means we don't necessarily know the provider. This allows local providers like Ollama to work properly ([#8989](https://github.com/mastra-ai/mastra/pull/8989))

-   feat: inject schema context into main agent for processor mode structured output ([#8886](https://github.com/mastra-ai/mastra/pull/8886))

-   Added providerOptions types to generate/stream for main builtin model router providers (openai/anthropic/google/xai) ([#8995](https://github.com/mastra-ai/mastra/pull/8995))

-   Generate a title for Agent.network() threads ([#8853](https://github.com/mastra-ai/mastra/pull/8853))

issues.title: [DISCORD:1428243966310088724] Agent Network Streaming Issue (AI SDK v5)
issues.body:
This issue was created from Discord post: https://discord.com/channels/1309558646228779139/1428243966310088724

Hi guys, I have old production app (50K+ users) that I am trying to convert to AI assistent chat bot. I have built a working versionwith Vercel AI SDK, but decided to migrate to Mastra (greedy). **Stuck for 3 weeks on `agent.network()` streaming.** Streaming is still broken after 0.21 upgrade. Need guidance urgently - my option is to revert to AI SDK but that wastes 3 weeks of migration work. Really want to stay with Mastra.

## Setup
- Mastra 0.21.0 + AI SDK v5, orchestrator with 8 sub-agents (Gmail, SEO, Sheets, Calendar, Ghost, Web, Voting, General), OpenRouter gpt-4o-mini

```typescript
const networkStream = await orchestrator.network(content, options);
for await (const part of toAISdkFormat(networkStream, { from: 'network' })) {
    writer.write(part);
}
```

## What We Observe

### ✅ What Works
- Agent routing is flawless - orchestrator correctly identifies and delegates to appropriate sub-agents
- Sub-agents execute successfully - tools called, operations completed
- Terminal logs show proper execution flow: orchestrator → sub-agent → tool execution → completion

### ❌ Streaming Issues

**1. No text-delta chunks during execution**
```
[CHAT-API] 📊 Stream iteration complete, chunks: 21 text collected: 0 chars
```
- Stream only emits `data-network` metadata chunks
- Zero `text-delta` chunks throughout entire execution
- No real-time text updates to UI

**2. Text only available after full completion**
```typescript
const networkResult = await networkStream.result;
console.log(networkResult?.result?.result); // Contains actual response text
```
- Text appears in `networkResult.result.result` path
- Arrives as single blob after all agents finish
- Not streamed incrementally

**3. Frontend receives raw metadata**
```typescript
// chat.tsx - had to add this filtering
onData: (dataPart) => {
    if (dataPart.type === 'data-network') {
        return; // Filter out or UI shows raw JSON objects
    }
}
```
- Without filtering, UI displays raw `data-network` JSON
- After page refresh, database-saved chunks appear as `[object Object]` in UI

## Current Workaround

```typescript
// Extract text after stream completes
if (!finalOutput) {
    const networkResult = await networkStream.result;
    const finalText = networkResult?.result?.result;

    if (finalText && typeof finalText === 'string') {
        writer.write({ type: 'text-delta', delta: finalText, id: messageId });
    }
}
```

This works but defeats the purpose of streaming - user sees nothing until full execution completes.

## Questions

1. **Is `agent.network()` designed to stream text-delta chunks in real-time?**
   - Or is it purely for internal routing with final result extraction?
   - Should we expect incremental text updates during sub-agent execution?

2. **What should `data-network` chunks contain and how should they be handled?**
   - Should these be filtered from UI display?
   - Are they being saved to database incorrectly?
   - Should they only be used internally by Mastra?

3. **Are we using the right API for UI streaming?**
   - Should multi-agent streaming use `agent.stream()` with manual routing logic instead?
   - Is `network()` intended for backend orchestration only?

4. **What's the expected data flow?**
   - Should orchestrator stream its own "thinking" text while routing?
   - Should sub-agent responses be streamed back through the network stream?
   - Or is the pattern: route silently → extract final result → display?

## What We Need

Confirmation on the intended streaming behavior of `agent.network()` for real-time UI updates. The routing works perfectly - just trying to understand if we're using the right API pattern for streaming multi-agent responses to users.

<@932127059461963866> <@1325823071558307895> I would really appreciate your assistance on this. 🙏

issues.title: [DISCORD:1431788598902132787] Bug in Parallel Workflow State Management
issues.body:
This issue was created from Discord post: https://discord.com/channels/1309558646228779139/1431788598902132787

## Summary
When resuming suspended `.parallel()` workflows sequentially while others run, completed workflows revert from `"success"` to `"suspended"`, blocking the next step.

## Bug
**Expected:** All parallel workflows complete → next step runs
**Actual:** Completed workflows revert to suspended → next step never runs

Resuming sequentially:
1. Resume subworkflow1 → `success` ✅
2. Resume subworkflow2 → `success` ✅
3. Resume subworkflow3 → **BUG**: subworkflow1 & 2 revert to `suspended` ❌

Console output:
```
subworkflow1: suspended ❌ (was success!)
subworkflow2: suspended ❌ (was success!)
subworkflow3: success
step3: not started ❌
```

## Root Cause
Race condition when parallel workflows:
- Suspend at different times
- Are resumed while others still running
- Mastra reverts completed ones to "suspended"

Trigger sequence:
1. Workflow A: suspend → resume → complete
2. Workflow B: suspend (C running) → resume → complete
3. Workflow C: suspend → resume → **BUG**: A & B revert to suspended

## Workaround
Wait for ALL to suspend before resuming. Bug only occurs when resuming while others running.

## Impact
Blocks production use with:
- Different execution times per branch
- Human-in-the-loop per branch
- Final synthesis after all complete
